description: About Me: I’m a business student at Harvard University with a deep fascination for space exploration, commercial space applications, and turning complex data into real-world impact. Alongside my background in strategy, research, project management, and storytelling, I’m genuinely passionate about space and excited to collaborate on a project that puts NASA’s open data to practical use.
summary: Wall-Life is an interactive Sims-Strategy Mars simulator that transforms NASA mission planning into an engaging game. Players create colonists, build a self-sustaining Martian habitat, and manage resources like power, water, oxygen, and food while balancing budgets, risks, and crew well-being. By making complex space engineering concepts accessible and fun, Wall-Life encourages critical thinking and inspires interest in space exploration.
details:
What Does It Do and How Does It Work?

Build, survive, and thrive on the Red Planet, 30 Sols at a time.

Wall-Life is an interactive, Sims-style Mars habitat simulator that puts players in the boots of a NASA mission planner. From pre-launch prep to boots on the ground, every choice carries real engineering consequences:

  • Assemble Your Crew: Customize your pioneer, select an authentic NASA career path, and build a multidisciplinary team.
  • Scout Real Martian Terrain: Choose from iconic landing sites (Jezero Crater, Arcadia Planitia, or Gale Crater) modeled using real surface imagery, radar, and subsurface water-ice mapping from the NASA Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (MRO): HiRISE & SHARAD, NASA Mars 2020 Perseverance Rover (Jezero Crater), NASA Mars Science Laboratory Curiosity Rover (Gale Crater), NASA Mars Odyssey Mission (Subsurface Water Ice Mapping), and the ESA ExoMars Trace Gas Orbiter (Martian Atmosphere & Subsurface Water).
  • Master the 30-Sol Challenge: Construct habitats, deploy power grids, and manage life-sustaining resources across 30 Martian days (Sols) while responding to real environmental conditions informed by the NASA Curiosity Rover Environmental Monitoring Station (REMS).
  • Balance High-Stakes Trade-Offs: Juggle strict mission budgets, available cargo mass, power supply, resource recycling, and crew well-being. Succeeding on Mars takes more than advanced hardware; it requires building a safe, sustainable, and comfortable home for humans to live.
Visual Reference 1 (Martian Subsurface Water Ice & Landing Terrain): Modeled after the SWIM Subsurface Water Ice Map and orbital photography from MRO HiRISE, Perseverance, and Curiosity.

What Benefits Does It Have?

Turn complex aerospace engineering into hands-on intuition.

Powered by open datasets from the NASA Open Data Portal and grounded in the NASA Systems Engineering Handbook (NASA/SP-2007-6105), NASA Environmental Control and Life Support System (ECLSS), NASA Human Integration Design Handbook (HIDH), Kilopower, ISRU, and MOXIE, Wall-Life bridges the gap between dense technical manuals and accessible gameplay:

  • Learn by Surviving: Instead of memorizing technical specs, players watch in real time how limited supplies, power failures, or sudden solar storms directly impact oxygen levels, habitat temperature, and crew survival.
  • Fail Fast, Iterate Faster: Provides a zero-risk sandbox where students can experiment with different habitat designs, learn from catastrophic mistakes, and optimize their mission decisions.
Visual Reference 2 (Closed-Loop Life Support Hardware): Resource recycling loops, water recovery, and oxygen generation mechanics mirror the systems documented in NASA ECLSS and the NASA Systems Engineering Handbook.

What Is the Intended Impact of the Project?

Democratizing space mission design for the next generation of explorers.

You don't need an engineering background to think like a mission architect. Wall-Life builds critical thinking and problem-solving skills by showing how engineers, botanists, medical professionals, and mission planners must collaborate to keep a settlement running.

  • Built to Scale: Aligned with the NASA Moon to Mars Architecture and JAXA Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) & Space Habitat Research, Wall-Life is designed to grow into a broader educational platform. Future updates will introduce lunar bases, multiplayer crew simulations, and interactive STEM classroom activities that inspire students everywhere to see themselves in the future of space exploration.

How Is Your Project Creative?

Where The Sims meets NASA Systems Engineering.

Most space games focus on piloting rockets; Wall-Life focuses on the human reality of living off-world by tying international aerospace research directly to daily crew needs:

  • Science Meets Life-Sim Gameplay: Blends authentic engineering constraints from CSA Mars Exploration & Autonomous Habitat Systems and the JAXA Space Exploration Innovation Hub (Closed-Loop Habitat & ISRU Research) with approachable, everyday habitat management.
  • Deep Character & Crew Dynamics: Players customize pioneers, build interpersonal relationships, and establish daily routines.
  • Closed-Loop Food & Human Survival: Models crew happiness, physical health, nutrition, and sustainable food production inspired by the NASA Vegetable Production System (Veggie) & Space Crop Production, the ESA MELiSSA Project (Closed-Loop Ecological Life Support), and DLR EDEN ISS (Closed-Loop Space Greenhouse & Hydroponics Research).
  • Cause-and-Effect Storytelling: Demonstrates how power, food, and water management directly govern the crew's daily safety and comfort, making space exploration engaging, enjoyable, and memorable.
Visual Reference 3 (Space Crop Production & Aeroponic Greenhouses): In-game hydroponic modules and lighting cycles draw directly from NASA Veggie, ESA MELiSSA, and the DLR EDEN ISS Greenhouse.

What Factors Did Your Team Consider?

Balancing hard science, human psychology, and universal accessibility.
  • Authentic NASA Constraints: Modeled real-world mission bottlenecks, including launch mass limits, power budgets, closed-loop life support (ECLSS), and space weather hazards, while translating them into intuitive visual mechanics.
  • The Human Element: Grounded crew psychology, sleep cycles, nutrition, and isolation dynamics in research from the NASA Human Research Program (HRP) and the NASA Human Integration Design Handbook (HIDH), recognizing that hardware alone cannot sustain a colony.
  • Zero-Barrier Accessibility: Engineered the simulator to run natively in any standard web browser with no downloads or specialized hardware required, ensuring anyone with an internet connection can play.
Visual Reference 4 (Human Factors & Crew Well-Being): Habitat spatial layouts, ergonomic workstations, and crew health monitoring reference human-factors standards from the NASA Human Integration Design Handbook (HIDH) and NASA Human Research Program (HRP).

Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware, and Software Used

  • Core Web Stack (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript): Built the interactive simulation engine, UI layout, and responsive browser gameplay from scratch.
  • Claude: Assisted with code debugging, refining simulation logic, and structuring technical architecture.
  • Google Sites: Publicly hosted the live web application for instant, browser-based access.
  • Google Gemini: Brainstormed core game mechanics, mapped NASA engineering principles to gameplay loops, assisted with prototype coding, and generated the introductory story and demonstration video.
  • ChatGPT: Refined written copy, organized project documentation, and clarified technical explanations.
  • Canva: Designed the pitch deck, visual assets, and presentation slides.
  • Google One: Managed cloud storage, version organization, and team project files.
  • Consumer Laptops & Tablets: Developed, stress-tested, and ran the simulator on everyday devices to guarantee smooth performance without specialized hardware.
